        # We'll convert "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" to "2023-10-10 13:55:36"

        # Parse the log time format
        # Example: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        # Split on ':' to separate date and time parts
        parts = time_part.split(':')
        date_part = parts[0]  # "10/Oct/2023"
        time_part = ':'.join(parts[1:])  # "13:55:36"
        
        day, month_str, year = date_part.split('/')
        hour, minute, second = time_part.split(':')
        
        # Convert month name to number
        month_map = {
            'Jan': '01', 'Feb': '02', 'Mar': '03', 'Apr': '04',
            'May': '05', 'Jun': '06', 'Jul': '07', 'Aug': '08',
            'Sep': '09', 'Oct': '10', 'Nov': '11', 'Dec': '12'
        }
        month = month_map[month_str]
        
        # Format as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
        log_time_formatted = f"{year}-{month}-{day} {hour}:{minute}:{second}"
        
        # Compare with start and end times
        if start <= log_time_formatted < end:
            result.append(entry)
    
    return result

    """Convert a percentage to a letter grade.
    
    Args:
        percent: The percentage score (or None)
        
    Returns:
        The letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) or "-" if percent is None
    """
    if percent is None:
        return "-"
    elif percent >= 90:
        return "A"
    elif percent >= 80:
        return "B"
    elif percent >= 70:
        return "C"
    elif percent >= 60:
        return "D"
    else:
        return "F"

    # Create a gradebook
    g = Gradebook()
    
    # Add students
    g.add_student("Alice")

    # Add assignments with categories
    g.add_assignment("Homework 1", 100, "homework")
    g.add_assignment("Homework 2", 100, "homework")
    g.add_assignment("Quiz 1", 50, "quiz")
    g.add_assignment("Exam 1", 200, "exam")
    
    # Set weights
    g.set_weight("homework", 0.4)
    g.set_weight("quiz", 0.3)
    g.set_weight("exam", 0.3)
    
    # Record scores
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 1", 85)
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 2", 90)
    g.record("Alice", "Quiz 1", 40)
    g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 180)
    
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 1", 70)
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 2", 75)
    g.record("Bob", "Quiz 1", 30)
    g.record("Bob", "Exam 1", 160)
    
    # Test weighted averages
    alice_percent = g.percent("Alice")
    bob_percent = g.percent("Bob")
    
    print(f"Alice's weighted percent: {alice_percent}")
    print(f"Bob's weighted percent: {bob_percent}")
    
    # Verify that the weighted averages are calculated correctly
    # Alice: homework avg = (85+90)/2 = 87.5, quiz avg = 40/50 = 80, exam avg = 180/200 = 90
    # Weighted: 87.5*0.4 + 80*0.3 + 90*0.3 = 35 + 24 + 27 = 86
    expected_alice = 86.0
    assert alice_percent == expected_alice, f"Expected {expected_alice}, got {alice_percent}"
    
    # Bob: homework avg = (70+75)/2 = 72.5, quiz avg = 30/50 = 60, exam avg = 160/200 = 80
    # Weighted: 72.5*0.4 + 60*0.3 + 80*0.3 = 29 + 18 + 24 = 71
    expected_bob = 71.0
    assert bob_percent == expected_bob, f"Expected {expected_bob}, got {bob_percent}"
    
    # Test with default category (should work the same as before)

    g2.add_student("Charlie")
    g2.add_assignment("Test 1", 100)
    g2.add_assignment("Test 2", 100)
    g2.record("Charlie", "Test 1", 80)
    g2.record("Charlie", "Test 2", 90)

    print("All category tests passed!")

def test_percentile():

        {'seconds': 1.0},

        {'seconds': 3.0},

        {'seconds': 5.0}

    # 25th percentile should be 2.0
    assert percentile(entries, 25) == 2.0
    
    # 75th percentile should be 4.0
    assert percentile(entries, 75) == 4.0
    
    # 100th percentile should be 5.0
    assert percentile(entries, 100) == 5.0
    
    # 1st percentile should be 1.0
    assert percentile(entries, 1) == 1.0
    
    # Test with duplicate values
    entries2 = [
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 3.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile should be 2.0
    assert percentile(entries2, 50) == 2.0
    
    # Test with larger dataset
    entries3 = [
        {'seconds': 0.1},
        {'seconds': 0.2},
        {'seconds': 0.3},
        {'seconds': 0.4},
        {'seconds': 0.5},
        {'seconds': 0.6},
        {'seconds': 0.7},
        {'seconds': 0.8},
        {'seconds': 0.9},
        {'seconds': 1.0}

    # 90th percentile should be 0.9

import re
from collections import Counter
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def parse_line(line):
    # Apache access log format: ip - - [time] "request" status bytes time
    # Example: 127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
    
    pattern = r'^(\S+) \S+ \S+ \[([^\]]+)\] "(\S+ \S+ \S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)$'
    match = re.match(pattern, line.strip())
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match expected format")
    
    ip, time, request, status, bytes_str, seconds = match.groups()
    
    # Parse request into method and path
    method, path, _ = request.split(' ')
    
    # Convert status to int
    status = int(status)
    
    # Convert bytes to int, handling "-" case
    if bytes_str == "-":
        bytes_val = 0
    else:
        bytes_val = int(bytes_str)
    
    # Convert seconds to float
    seconds = float(seconds)
    
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes_val,
        'seconds': seconds
    }
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All tests passed!")
def parse_log(text):
    """Parse log text and return list of parsed dicts for valid lines."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parsed = parse_line(line)
            result.append(parsed)
        except ValueError:
            # Skip malformed lines
            continue
    
    return result

def bad_lines(text):
    """Return 1-based line numbers of malformed lines that are not blank."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):  # 1-based indexing
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            result.append(i)
    
    return result

def status_counts(entries):
    """Return a dictionary mapping status codes to their counts."""
    counts = {}
    for entry in entries:
        status = entry['status']
        counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
    return counts

def error_rate(entries):
    """Return the fraction of entries whose status is 500 or more, rounded to 4 decimals.
    
    Returns 0.0 when there are no entries.
    """
    if not entries:
        return 0.0
    
    error_count = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if entry['status'] >= 500:
            error_count += 1
    
    return round(error_count / len(entries), 4)

def top_paths(entries, n=3):
    """Return a list of (path, count) tuples for the n most requested paths.
    
    Paths with query strings are stripped of the query part.
    Ties are broken by path name (lexicographically).
    """
    # Extract paths from entries
    paths = []
    for entry in entries:
        path = entry['path']
        # Remove query string if present
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        clean_path = parsed.path
        paths.append(clean_path)
    
    # Count occurrences
    counter = Counter(paths)
    
    # Get most common items
    most_common = counter.most_common(n)
    
    # If there are ties, sort by path name
    if most_common:
        # Group by count value
        groups = {}
        for path, count in most_common:
            if count not in groups:
                groups[count] = []
            groups[count].append(path)
        
        # Sort each group lexicographically
        for count in groups:
            groups[count].sort()
        
        # Build result in order of count (descending) then path (ascending)
        result = []
        for count in sorted(groups.keys(), reverse=True):
            for path in groups[count]:
                result.append((path, count))
        
        return result
    
    return []

def percentile(entries, p):
    """Return the p-th percentile of the seconds values by nearest rank.
    
    The smallest value such that at least p percent of the values are less than or equal to it.
    Raises ValueError unless 0 < p <= 100 and there is at least one value.
    """
    if not entries:
        raise ValueError("No entries provided")
    
    if not (0 < p <= 100):
        raise ValueError("p must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 100")
    
    # Extract seconds values
    seconds_values = [entry['seconds'] for entry in entries]
    
    # Sort the values
    sorted_values = sorted(seconds_values)
    
    # Calculate the rank
    n = len(sorted_values)
    rank = (p / 100.0) * n
    
    # Find the nearest rank (smallest value such that at least p percent are <= it)
    # If rank is an integer, we want the value at that index
    # If rank is not an integer, we want the value at the next integer index
    if rank.is_integer():
        # Exact match - return the value at that index
        index = int(rank) - 1  # Convert to 0-based index
    else:
        # Round up to nearest integer to get the "nearest rank"
        index = int(rank)  # This gives us the next higher rank
    
    # Ensure index is within bounds
    if index >= n:
        index = n - 1
    
    return sorted_values[index]

    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    # Test new parse_log function
    test_log = '''127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
invalid line format
192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123

10.0.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:15:00:00 +0000] "PUT /upload HTTP/1.1" 200 1024 0.050'''
    
    parsed = parse_log(test_log)
    assert len(parsed) == 3, f"Expected 3 parsed lines, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]['ip'] == '127.0.0.1'
    assert parsed[1]['ip'] == '192.168.1.1'
    assert parsed[2]['ip'] == '10.0.0.1'
    
    # Test bad_lines function
    bad_line_nums = bad_lines(test_log)
    assert bad_line_nums == [2], f"Expected [2], got {bad_line_nums}"
    
    # Test with all blank lines
    blank_log = '''
    
    '''
    parsed_blank = parse_log(blank_log)
    assert len(parsed_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 parsed lines, got {len(parsed_blank)}"
    bad_blank = bad_lines(blank_log)
    assert len(bad_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 bad lines, got {len(bad_blank)}"

    # Test top_paths function
    test_entries = [
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/index.html?param=value'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/api/data'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/about?filter=active'},
    ]
    
    result = top_paths(test_entries, n=3)
    # All three paths have 3 occurrences, so sort by path name
    expected = [('/about', 3), ('/contact', 3), ('/index.html', 3)]
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with ties - should sort by path name
    test_entries_ties = [
        {'path': '/z'},
        {'path': '/a'},
        {'path': '/z'},
        {'path': '/a'},
        {'path': '/b'},
        {'path': '/b'},
    ]
    
    result_ties = top_paths(test_entries_ties, n=3)
    expected_ties = [('/a', 2), ('/b', 2), ('/z', 2)]
    assert result_ties == expected_ties, f"Expected {expected_ties}, got {result_ties}"
    
    print("All tests passed!")
    print("top_paths tests passed!")
def between(entries, start, end):
    """
    Return entries whose time t satisfies start <= t < end.
    start and end are "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" strings.
    """
    # Convert the start and end times to the format used in the log entries
    # The log format is "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
    # We'll need to parse and compare these times
    
    # For simplicity, we'll assume the entries are already sorted by time
    # and we'll do a simple string comparison since the format is consistent
    
    result = []
    for entry in entries:
        time_str = entry['time']
        # Extract just the date/time part (before the timezone)
        # Format: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
        # We want to compare "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" with our start/end times
        time_part = time_str.split(' ')[0]  # This gets "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        
        # Convert the log time format to a comparable format
        # We'll convert "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" to "2023-10-10 13:55:36"
        # This is a bit tricky because we have to parse the month name
        
        # Parse the log time format
        # Example: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        # Split on ':' to separate date and time parts
        parts = time_part.split(':')
        date_part = parts[0]  # "10/Oct/2023"
        time_part = ':'.join(parts[1:])  # "13:55:36"
        
        day, month_str, year = date_part.split('/')
        hour, minute, second = time_part.split(':')
        
        # Convert month name to number
        month_map = {
            'Jan': '01', 'Feb': '02', 'Mar': '03', 'Apr': '04',
            'May': '05', 'Jun': '06', 'Jul': '07', 'Aug': '08',
            'Sep': '09', 'Oct': '10', 'Nov': '11', 'Dec': '12'
        }
        month = month_map[month_str]
        
        # Format as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
        log_time_formatted = f"{year}-{month}-{day} {hour}:{minute}:{second}"
        
        # Compare with start and end times
        if start <= log_time_formatted < end:
            result.append(entry)
    
    return result

Double quotes in URLs are escaped as ". """ def replace_link(match): text_content = match.group(1) url_content = match.group(2) # Escape double quotes in URL escaped_url = url_content.replace('"', '"') return f'{text_content}' # Find all [text](url) patterns link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' result = re.sub(link_pattern, replace_link, text) return result def to_html(text): """ Convert markdown text to HTML paragraphs. Blocks separated by blank lines become

...

paragraphs. Lines inside a block are joined with one space. Blocks are joined with "\\n". HTML characters &, <, > are escaped. Headings (# text) become

tags. Emphasis (**text** becomes text, *text* becomes text) Links [text](url) become text Ordered lists (1. , 2. , etc.) become

def letter_grade(percent):
    """Convert a percentage to a letter grade.
    
    Args:
        percent: The percentage score (or None)
        
    Returns:
        The letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) or "-" if percent is None
    """
    if percent is None:
        return "-"
    elif percent >= 90:
        return "A"
    elif percent >= 80:
        return "B"
    elif percent >= 70:
        return "C"
    elif percent >= 60:
        return "D"
    else:
        return "F"

from s8_grades import Gradebook

def test_categories():
    # Create a gradebook
    g = Gradebook()
    
    # Add students
    g.add_student("Alice")
    g.add_student("Bob")
    
    # Add assignments with categories
    g.add_assignment("Homework 1", 100, "homework")
    g.add_assignment("Homework 2", 100, "homework")
    g.add_assignment("Quiz 1", 50, "quiz")
    g.add_assignment("Exam 1", 200, "exam")
    
    # Set weights
    g.set_weight("homework", 0.4)
    g.set_weight("quiz", 0.3)
    g.set_weight("exam", 0.3)
    
    # Record scores
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 1", 85)
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 2", 90)
    g.record("Alice", "Quiz 1", 40)
    g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 180)
    
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 1", 70)
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 2", 75)
    g.record("Bob", "Quiz 1", 30)
    g.record("Bob", "Exam 1", 160)
    
    # Test weighted averages
    alice_percent = g.percent("Alice")
    bob_percent = g.percent("Bob")
    
    print(f"Alice's weighted percent: {alice_percent}")
    print(f"Bob's weighted percent: {bob_percent}")
    
    # Verify that the weighted averages are calculated correctly
    # Alice: homework avg = (85+90)/2 = 87.5, quiz avg = 40/50 = 80, exam avg = 180/200 = 90
    # Weighted: 87.5*0.4 + 80*0.3 + 90*0.3 = 35 + 24 + 27 = 86
    expected_alice = 86.0
    assert alice_percent == expected_alice, f"Expected {expected_alice}, got {alice_percent}"
    
    # Bob: homework avg = (70+75)/2 = 72.5, quiz avg = 30/50 = 60, exam avg = 160/200 = 80
    # Weighted: 72.5*0.4 + 60*0.3 + 80*0.3 = 29 + 18 + 24 = 71
    expected_bob = 71.0
    assert bob_percent == expected_bob, f"Expected {expected_bob}, got {bob_percent}"
    
    # Test with default category (should work the same as before)
    g2 = Gradebook()
    g2.add_student("Charlie")
    g2.add_assignment("Test 1", 100)
    g2.add_assignment("Test 2", 100)
    g2.record("Charlie", "Test 1", 80)
    g2.record("Charlie", "Test 2", 90)
    
    charlie_percent = g2.percent("Charlie")
    print(f"Charlie's percent (default category): {charlie_percent}")
    
    # Should be simple average: (80+90)/2 = 85
    assert charlie_percent == 85.0, f"Expected 85.0, got {charlie_percent}"
    
    print("All category tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_categories()

from s2_logs import percentile, parse_log

def test_percentile():
    # Test with simple case
    entries = [
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 3.0},
        {'seconds': 4.0},
        {'seconds': 5.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile (median) should be 3.0
    assert percentile(entries, 50) == 3.0
    
    # 25th percentile should be 2.0
    assert percentile(entries, 25) == 2.0
    
    # 75th percentile should be 4.0
    assert percentile(entries, 75) == 4.0
    
    # 100th percentile should be 5.0
    assert percentile(entries, 100) == 5.0
    
    # 1st percentile should be 1.0
    assert percentile(entries, 1) == 1.0
    
    # Test with duplicate values
    entries2 = [
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 3.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile should be 2.0
    assert percentile(entries2, 50) == 2.0
    
    # Test with larger dataset
    entries3 = [
        {'seconds': 0.1},
        {'seconds': 0.2},
        {'seconds': 0.3},
        {'seconds': 0.4},
        {'seconds': 0.5},
        {'seconds': 0.6},
        {'seconds': 0.7},
        {'seconds': 0.8},
        {'seconds': 0.9},
        {'seconds': 1.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile should be 0.5
    assert percentile(entries3, 50) == 0.5
    
    # 90th percentile should be 0.9
    assert percentile(entries3, 90) == 0.9
    
    # Test error conditions
    try:
        percentile([], 50)
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    try:
        percentile(entries, 0)
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    try:
        percentile(entries, 101)
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All percentile tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_percentile()

# Test 1: Basic functionality
print("Test 1: Basic functionality")
g.add_student("Alice")
g.add_student("Bob")
g.add_assignment("Homework 1", 100)
g.add_assignment("Exam 1", 200)

g.record("Alice", "Homework 1", 85)
g.record("Bob", "Homework 1", 92)
g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 180)

# Curve with positive points
changed = g.curve("Homework 1", 5)
print(f"Changed {changed} scores (expected: 2)")
print(f"Alice Homework 1: {g.score('Alice', 'Homework 1')} (expected: 90)")
print(f"Bob Homework 1: {g.score('Bob', 'Homework 1')} (expected: 97)")

# Curve with negative points
changed = g.curve("Homework 1", -10)
print(f"Changed {changed} scores (expected: 2)")
print(f"Alice Homework 1: {g.score('Alice', 'Homework 1')} (expected: 80)")
print(f"Bob Homework 1: {g.score('Bob', 'Homework 1')} (expected: 87)")

# Test 2: Capping at max_points
print("\nTest 2: Capping at max_points")
g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 190)  # Close to max of 200
changed = g.curve("Exam 1", 20)  # Would go over max
print(f"Changed {changed} scores (expected: 1)")
print(f"Alice Exam 1: {g.score('Alice', 'Exam 1')} (expected: 200)")

# Test 3: No change when points don't affect scores
print("\nTest 3: No change when points don't affect scores")
g.record("Alice", "Homework 1", 100)  # Already at max
changed = g.curve("Homework 1", 5)  # Should not change anything
print(f"Changed {changed} scores (expected: 0)")
print(f"Alice Homework 1: {g.score('Alice', 'Homework 1')} (expected: 100)")

# Test 4: Error handling
print("\nTest 4: Error handling")
try:
    g.curve("NonExistent", 10)
    print("ERROR: Should have raised KeyError")
except KeyError:
    print("Correctly raised KeyError for unknown assignment")

print("\nAll tests completed successfully!")

import re
from collections import Counter
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def parse_line(line):
    # Apache access log format: ip - - [time] "request" status bytes time
    # Example: 127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
    
    pattern = r'^(\S+) \S+ \S+ \[([^\]]+)\] "(\S+ \S+ \S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)$'
    match = re.match(pattern, line.strip())
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match expected format")
    
    ip, time, request, status, bytes_str, seconds = match.groups()
    
    # Parse request into method and path
    method, path, _ = request.split(' ')
    
    # Convert status to int
    status = int(status)
    
    # Convert bytes to int, handling "-" case
    if bytes_str == "-":
        bytes_val = 0
    else:
        bytes_val = int(bytes_str)
    
    # Convert seconds to float
    seconds = float(seconds)
    
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes_val,
        'seconds': seconds
    }
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All tests passed!")
def parse_log(text):
    """Parse log text and return list of parsed dicts for valid lines."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parsed = parse_line(line)
            result.append(parsed)
        except ValueError:
            # Skip malformed lines
            continue
    
    return result

def bad_lines(text):
    """Return 1-based line numbers of malformed lines that are not blank."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):  # 1-based indexing
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            result.append(i)
    
    return result

def status_counts(entries):
    """Return a dictionary mapping status codes to their counts."""
    counts = {}
    for entry in entries:
        status = entry['status']
        counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
    return counts

def error_rate(entries):
    """Return the fraction of entries whose status is 500 or more, rounded to 4 decimals.
    
    Returns 0.0 when there are no entries.
    """
    if not entries:
        return 0.0
    
    error_count = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if entry['status'] >= 500:
            error_count += 1
    
    return round(error_count / len(entries), 4)

def top_paths(entries, n=3):
    """Return a list of (path, count) tuples for the n most requested paths.
    
    Paths with query strings are stripped of the query part.
    Ties are broken by path name (lexicographically).
    """
    # Extract paths from entries
    paths = []
    for entry in entries:
        path = entry['path']
        # Remove query string if present
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        clean_path = parsed.path
        paths.append(clean_path)
    
    # Count occurrences
    counter = Counter(paths)
    
    # Get most common items
    most_common = counter.most_common(n)
    
    # If there are ties, sort by path name
    if most_common:
        # Group by count value
        groups = {}
        for path, count in most_common:
            if count not in groups:
                groups[count] = []
            groups[count].append(path)
        
        # Sort each group lexicographically
        for count in groups:
            groups[count].sort()
        
        # Build result in order of count (descending) then path (ascending)
        result = []
        for count in sorted(groups.keys(), reverse=True):
            for path in groups[count]:
                result.append((path, count))
        
        return result
    
    return []

def percentile(entries, p):
    """Return the p-th percentile of the seconds values by nearest rank.
    
    The smallest value such that at least p percent of the values are less than or equal to it.
    Raises ValueError unless 0 < p <= 100 and there is at least one value.
    """
    if not entries:
        raise ValueError("No entries provided")
    
    if not (0 < p <= 100):
        raise ValueError("p must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 100")
    
    # Extract seconds values
    seconds_values = [entry['seconds'] for entry in entries]
    
    # Sort the values
    sorted_values = sorted(seconds_values)
    
    # Calculate the rank
    n = len(sorted_values)
    rank = (p / 100.0) * n
    
    # Find the nearest rank (smallest value such that at least p percent are <= it)
    # If rank is an integer, we want the value at that index
    # If rank is not an integer, we want the value at the next integer index
    if rank.is_integer():
        # Exact match - return the value at that index
        index = int(rank) - 1  # Convert to 0-based index
    else:
        # Round up to nearest integer to get the "nearest rank"
        index = int(rank)  # This gives us the next higher rank
    
    # Ensure index is within bounds
    if index >= n:
        index = n - 1
    
    return sorted_values[index]
# Test the new functions
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    # Test new parse_log function
    test_log = '''127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
invalid line format
192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123

10.0.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:15:00:00 +0000] "PUT /upload HTTP/1.1" 200 1024 0.050'''
    
    parsed = parse_log(test_log)
    assert len(parsed) == 3, f"Expected 3 parsed lines, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]['ip'] == '127.0.0.1'
    assert parsed[1]['ip'] == '192.168.1.1'
    assert parsed[2]['ip'] == '10.0.0.1'
    
    # Test bad_lines function
    bad_line_nums = bad_lines(test_log)
    assert bad_line_nums == [2], f"Expected [2], got {bad_line_nums}"
    
    # Test with all blank lines
    blank_log = '''
    
    '''
    parsed_blank = parse_log(blank_log)
    assert len(parsed_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 parsed lines, got {len(parsed_blank)}"
    bad_blank = bad_lines(blank_log)
    assert len(bad_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 bad lines, got {len(bad_blank)}"

    # Test top_paths function
    test_entries = [
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/index.html?param=value'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/api/data'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/about?filter=active'},
    ]
    
    result = top_paths(test_entries, n=3)
    # All three paths have 3 occurrences, so sort by path name
    expected = [('/about', 3), ('/contact', 3), ('/index.html', 3)]
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with ties - should sort by path name

    assert result_ties == expected_ties, f"Expected {expected_ties}, got {result_ties}"
    
    print("All tests passed!")
    print("top_paths tests passed!")
def between(entries, start, end):
    """
    Return entries whose time t satisfies start <= t < end.
    start and end are "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" strings.
    """
    # Convert the start and end times to the format used in the log entries
    # The log format is "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
    # We'll need to parse and compare these times
    
    # For simplicity, we'll assume the entries are already sorted by time
    # and we'll do a simple string comparison since the format is consistent
    
    result = []
    for entry in entries:
        time_str = entry['time']
        # Extract just the date/time part (before the timezone)
        # Format: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
        # We want to compare "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" with our start/end times

    """Convert a percentage to a letter grade.
    
    Args:
        percent: The percentage score (or None)
        
    Returns:
        The letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) or "-" if percent is None
    """
    if percent is None:
        return "-"
    elif percent >= 90:
        return "A"
    elif percent >= 80:
        return "B"
    elif percent >= 70:
        return "C"
    elif percent >= 60:
        return "D"
    else:
        return "F"

#!/usr/bin/env python3

from s8_grades import Gradebook

def test_categories():
    # Create a gradebook
    g = Gradebook()
    
    # Add students
    g.add_student("Alice")
    g.add_student("Bob")
    
    # Add assignments with categories
    g.add_assignment("Homework 1", 100, "homework")
    g.add_assignment("Homework 2", 100, "homework")
    g.add_assignment("Quiz 1", 50, "quiz")
    g.add_assignment("Exam 1", 200, "exam")
    
    # Set weights
    g.set_weight("homework", 0.4)
    g.set_weight("quiz", 0.3)
    g.set_weight("exam", 0.3)
    
    # Record scores
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 1", 85)
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 2", 90)
    g.record("Alice", "Quiz 1", 40)
    g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 180)
    
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 1", 70)
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 2", 75)
    g.record("Bob", "Quiz 1", 30)
    g.record("Bob", "Exam 1", 160)
    
    # Test weighted averages
    alice_percent = g.percent("Alice")
    bob_percent = g.percent("Bob")
    
    print(f"Alice's weighted percent: {alice_percent}")
    print(f"Bob's weighted percent: {bob_percent}")
    
    # Verify that the weighted averages are calculated correctly
    # Alice: homework avg = (85+90)/2 = 87.5, quiz avg = 40/50 = 80, exam avg = 180/200 = 90
    # Weighted: 87.5*0.4 + 80*0.3 + 90*0.3 = 35 + 24 + 27 = 86
    expected_alice = 86.0
    assert alice_percent == expected_alice, f"Expected {expected_alice}, got {alice_percent}"
    
    # Bob: homework avg = (70+75)/2 = 72.5, quiz avg = 30/50 = 60, exam avg = 160/200 = 80
    # Weighted: 72.5*0.4 + 60*0.3 + 80*0.3 = 29 + 18 + 24 = 71
    expected_bob = 71.0
    assert bob_percent == expected_bob, f"Expected {expected_bob}, got {bob_percent}"
    
    # Test with default category (should work the same as before)
    g2 = Gradebook()
    g2.add_student("Charlie")
    g2.add_assignment("Test 1", 100)
    g2.add_assignment("Test 2", 100)
    g2.record("Charlie", "Test 1", 80)
    g2.record("Charlie", "Test 2", 90)
    
    charlie_percent = g2.percent("Charlie")
    print(f"Charlie's percent (default category): {charlie_percent}")
    
    # Should be simple average: (80+90)/2 = 85
    assert charlie_percent == 85.0, f"Expected 85.0, got {charlie_percent}"
    
    print("All category tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_categories()

from s2_logs import percentile, parse_log

def test_percentile():
    # Test with simple case
    entries = [
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 3.0},
        {'seconds': 4.0},
        {'seconds': 5.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile (median) should be 3.0
    assert percentile(entries, 50) == 3.0
    
    # 25th percentile should be 2.0
    assert percentile(entries, 25) == 2.0
    
    # 75th percentile should be 4.0
    assert percentile(entries, 75) == 4.0
    
    # 100th percentile should be 5.0
    assert percentile(entries, 100) == 5.0
    
    # 1st percentile should be 1.0
    assert percentile(entries, 1) == 1.0
    
    # Test with duplicate values
    entries2 = [
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 3.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile should be 2.0
    assert percentile(entries2, 50) == 2.0
    
    # Test with larger dataset
    entries3 = [
        {'seconds': 0.1},
        {'seconds': 0.2},
        {'seconds': 0.3},
        {'seconds': 0.4},
        {'seconds': 0.5},
        {'seconds': 0.6},
        {'seconds': 0.7},
        {'seconds': 0.8},
        {'seconds': 0.9},
        {'seconds': 1.0}
    ]
    
    # 50th percentile should be 0.5
    assert percentile(entries3, 50) == 0.5
    
    # 90th percentile should be 0.9
    assert percentile(entries3, 90) == 0.9
    
    # Test error conditions
    try:
        percentile([], 50)
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    try:
        percentile(entries, 0)
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    try:
        percentile(entries, 101)
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All percentile tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_percentile()

import re
from collections import Counter
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def parse_line(line):
    # Apache access log format: ip - - [time] "request" status bytes time
    # Example: 127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
    
    pattern = r'^(\S+) \S+ \S+ \[([^\]]+)\] "(\S+ \S+ \S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)$'
    match = re.match(pattern, line.strip())
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match expected format")
    
    ip, time, request, status, bytes_str, seconds = match.groups()
    
    # Parse request into method and path
    method, path, _ = request.split(' ')
    
    # Convert status to int
    status = int(status)
    
    # Convert bytes to int, handling "-" case
    if bytes_str == "-":
        bytes_val = 0
    else:
        bytes_val = int(bytes_str)
    
    # Convert seconds to float
    seconds = float(seconds)
    
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes_val,
        'seconds': seconds
    }
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All tests passed!")
def parse_log(text):
    """Parse log text and return list of parsed dicts for valid lines."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parsed = parse_line(line)
            result.append(parsed)
        except ValueError:
            # Skip malformed lines
            continue
    
    return result

def bad_lines(text):
    """Return 1-based line numbers of malformed lines that are not blank."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):  # 1-based indexing
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            result.append(i)
    
    return result

def status_counts(entries):
    """Return a dictionary mapping status codes to their counts."""
    counts = {}
    for entry in entries:
        status = entry['status']
        counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
    return counts

def error_rate(entries):
    """Return the fraction of entries whose status is 500 or more, rounded to 4 decimals.
    
    Returns 0.0 when there are no entries.
    """
    if not entries:
        return 0.0
    
    error_count = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if entry['status'] >= 500:
            error_count += 1
    
    return round(error_count / len(entries), 4)

def top_paths(entries, n=3):
    """Return a list of (path, count) tuples for the n most requested paths.
    
    Paths with query strings are stripped of the query part.
    Ties are broken by path name (lexicographically).
    """
    # Extract paths from entries
    paths = []
    for entry in entries:
        path = entry['path']
        # Remove query string if present
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        clean_path = parsed.path
        paths.append(clean_path)
    
    # Count occurrences
    counter = Counter(paths)
    
    # Get most common items
    most_common = counter.most_common(n)
    
    # If there are ties, sort by path name
    if most_common:
        # Group by count value
        groups = {}
        for path, count in most_common:
            if count not in groups:
                groups[count] = []
            groups[count].append(path)
        
        # Sort each group lexicographically
        for count in groups:
            groups[count].sort()
        
        # Build result in order of count (descending) then path (ascending)
        result = []
        for count in sorted(groups.keys(), reverse=True):
            for path in groups[count]:
                result.append((path, count))
        
        return result
    
    return []

def percentile(entries, p):
    """Return the p-th percentile of the seconds values by nearest rank.
    
    The smallest value such that at least p percent of the values are less than or equal to it.
    Raises ValueError unless 0 < p <= 100 and there is at least one value.
    """
    if not entries:
        raise ValueError("No entries provided")
    
    if not (0 < p <= 100):
        raise ValueError("p must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 100")
    
    # Extract seconds values
    seconds_values = [entry['seconds'] for entry in entries]
    
    # Sort the values
    sorted_values = sorted(seconds_values)
    
    # Calculate the rank
    n = len(sorted_values)
    rank = (p / 100.0) * n
    
    # Find the nearest rank (smallest value such that at least p percent are <= it)
    # If rank is an integer, we want the value at that index
    # If rank is not an integer, we want the value at the next integer index
    if rank.is_integer():
        # Exact match - return the value at that index
        index = int(rank) - 1  # Convert to 0-based index
    else:
        # Round up to nearest integer to get the "nearest rank"
        index = int(rank)  # This gives us the next higher rank
    
    # Ensure index is within bounds
    if index >= n:
        index = n - 1
    
    return sorted_values[index]
# Test the new functions
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    # Test new parse_log function
    test_log = '''127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045

    parsed = parse_log(test_log)
    assert len(parsed) == 3, f"Expected 3 parsed lines, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]['ip'] == '127.0.0.1'
    assert parsed[1]['ip'] == '192.168.1.1'
    assert parsed[2]['ip'] == '10.0.0.1'
    
    # Test bad_lines function
    bad_line_nums = bad_lines(test_log)
    assert bad_line_nums == [2], f"Expected [2], got {bad_line_nums}"
    
    # Test with all blank lines

    bad_blank = bad_lines(blank_log)
    assert len(bad_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 bad lines, got {len(bad_blank)}"

    """

    Args:
        percent: The percentage score (or None)
        
    Returns:
        The letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) or "-" if percent is None
    """
    if percent is None:
        return "-"
    elif percent >= 90:
        return "A"
    elif percent >= 80:
        return "B"
    elif percent >= 70:
        return "C"
    elif percent >= 60:
        return "D"
    else:
        return "F"

    g.set_weight("homework", 0.4)
    g.set_weight("quiz", 0.3)
    g.set_weight("exam", 0.3)
    
    # Record scores
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 1", 85)
    g.record("Alice", "Homework 2", 90)
    g.record("Alice", "Quiz 1", 40)
    g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 180)
    
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 1", 70)
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 2", 75)
    g.record("Bob", "Quiz 1", 30)
    g.record("Bob", "Exam 1", 160)
    
    # Test weighted averages
    alice_percent = g.percent("Alice")
    bob_percent = g.percent("Bob")

import re
from collections import Counter
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def parse_line(line):
    # Apache access log format: ip - - [time] "request" status bytes time
    # Example: 127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
    
    pattern = r'^(\S+) \S+ \S+ \[([^\]]+)\] "(\S+ \S+ \S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)$'
    match = re.match(pattern, line.strip())
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match expected format")
    
    ip, time, request, status, bytes_str, seconds = match.groups()
    
    # Parse request into method and path
    method, path, _ = request.split(' ')
    
    # Convert status to int
    status = int(status)
    
    # Convert bytes to int, handling "-" case
    if bytes_str == "-":
        bytes_val = 0
    else:
        bytes_val = int(bytes_str)
    
    # Convert seconds to float
    seconds = float(seconds)
    
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes_val,
        'seconds': seconds
    }
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All tests passed!")
def parse_log(text):
    """Parse log text and return list of parsed dicts for valid lines."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parsed = parse_line(line)
            result.append(parsed)
        except ValueError:
            # Skip malformed lines
            continue
    
    return result

def bad_lines(text):
    """Return 1-based line numbers of malformed lines that are not blank."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):  # 1-based indexing
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            result.append(i)
    
    return result

def status_counts(entries):
    """Return a dictionary mapping status codes to their counts."""
    counts = {}
    for entry in entries:
        status = entry['status']
        counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
    return counts

def error_rate(entries):
    """Return the fraction of entries whose status is 500 or more, rounded to 4 decimals.
    
    Returns 0.0 when there are no entries.
    """
    if not entries:
        return 0.0
    
    error_count = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if entry['status'] >= 500:
            error_count += 1
    
    return round(error_count / len(entries), 4)

def top_paths(entries, n=3):
    """Return a list of (path, count) tuples for the n most requested paths.
    
    Paths with query strings are stripped of the query part.
    Ties are broken by path name (lexicographically).
    """
    # Extract paths from entries
    paths = []
    for entry in entries:
        path = entry['path']
        # Remove query string if present
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        clean_path = parsed.path
        paths.append(clean_path)
    
    # Count occurrences
    counter = Counter(paths)
    
    # Get most common items
    most_common = counter.most_common(n)
    
    # If there are ties, sort by path name
    if most_common:
        # Group by count value
        groups = {}
        for path, count in most_common:
            if count not in groups:
                groups[count] = []
            groups[count].append(path)
        
        # Sort each group lexicographically
        for count in groups:
            groups[count].sort()
        
        # Build result in order of count (descending) then path (ascending)
        result = []
        for count in sorted(groups.keys(), reverse=True):
            for path in groups[count]:
                result.append((path, count))
        
        return result
    
    return []

def percentile(entries, p):
    """Return the p-th percentile of the seconds values by nearest rank.
    
    The smallest value such that at least p percent of the values are less than or equal to it.
    Raises ValueError unless 0 < p <= 100 and there is at least one value.
    """
    if not entries:
        raise ValueError("No entries provided")
    
    if not (0 < p <= 100):
        raise ValueError("p must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 100")
    
    # Extract seconds values
    seconds_values = [entry['seconds'] for entry in entries]
    
    # Sort the values
    sorted_values = sorted(seconds_values)
    
    # Calculate the rank
    n = len(sorted_values)
    rank = (p / 100.0) * n
    
    # Find the nearest rank (smallest value such that at least p percent are <= it)
    # If rank is an integer, we want the value at that index
    # If rank is not an integer, we want the value at the next integer index
    if rank.is_integer():
        # Exact match - return the value at that index
        index = int(rank) - 1  # Convert to 0-based index
    else:
        # Round up to nearest integer to get the "nearest rank"
        index = int(rank)  # This gives us the next higher rank
    
    # Ensure index is within bounds
    if index >= n:
        index = n - 1
    
    return sorted_values[index]

    # Test with the example line

    result = parse_line(test_line)

    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    # Test new parse_log function
    test_log = '''127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
invalid line format

10.0.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:15:00:00 +0000] "PUT /upload HTTP/1.1" 200 1024 0.050'''
    
    parsed = parse_log(test_log)
    assert len(parsed) == 3, f"Expected 3 parsed lines, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]['ip'] == '127.0.0.1'
    assert parsed[1]['ip'] == '192.168.1.1'
    assert parsed[2]['ip'] == '10.0.0.1'
    
    # Test bad_lines function
    bad_line_nums = bad_lines(test_log)
    assert bad_line_nums == [2], f"Expected [2], got {bad_line_nums}"
    
    # Test with all blank lines
    blank_log = '''
    
    '''
    parsed_blank = parse_log(blank_log)
    assert len(parsed_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 parsed lines, got {len(parsed_blank)}"
    bad_blank = bad_lines(blank_log)
    assert len(bad_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 bad lines, got {len(bad_blank)}"

    # Test top_paths function
    test_entries = [
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/index.html?param=value'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/api/data'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/about?filter=active'},
    ]
    
    result = top_paths(test_entries, n=3)
    # All three paths have 3 occurrences, so sort by path name
    expected = [('/about', 3), ('/contact', 3), ('/index.html', 3)]
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with ties - should sort by path name
    test_entries_ties = [
        {'path': '/z'},
        {'path': '/a'},

        {'path': '/b'},

    ]
    
    result_ties = top_paths(test_entries_ties, n=3)
    expected_ties = [('/a', 2), ('/b', 2), ('/z', 2)]
    assert result_ties == expected_ties, f"Expected {expected_ties}, got {result_ties}"
    
    print("All tests passed!")
    print("top_paths tests passed!")
def between(entries, start, end):
    """
    Return entries whose time t satisfies start <= t < end.
    start and end are "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" strings.
    """
    # Convert the start and end times to the format used in the log entries
    # The log format is "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
    # We'll need to parse and compare these times
    
    # For simplicity, we'll assume the entries are already sorted by time
    # and we'll do a simple string comparison since the format is consistent
    
    result = []
    for entry in entries:
        time_str = entry['time']
        # Extract just the date/time part (before the timezone)
        # Format: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
        # We want to compare "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" with our start/end times
        time_part = time_str.split(' ')[0]  # This gets "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        
        # Convert the log time format to a comparable format
        # We'll convert "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" to "2023-10-10 13:55:36"
        # This is a bit tricky because we have to parse the month name
        
        # Parse the log time format
        # Example: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        # Split on ':' to separate date and time parts
        parts = time_part.split(':')
        date_part = parts[0]  # "10/Oct/2023"
        time_part = ':'.join(parts[1:])  # "13:55:36"
        
        day, month_str, year = date_part.split('/')
        hour, minute, second = time_part.split(':')
        
        # Convert month name to number
        month_map = {
            'Jan': '01', 'Feb': '02', 'Mar': '03', 'Apr': '04',
            'May': '05', 'Jun': '06', 'Jul': '07', 'Aug': '08',
            'Sep': '09', 'Oct': '10', 'Nov': '11', 'Dec': '12'
        }
        month = month_map[month_str]
        
        # Format as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
        log_time_formatted = f"{year}-{month}-{day} {hour}:{minute}:{second}"
        
        # Compare with start and end times
        if start <= log_time_formatted < end:
            result.append(entry)

    """Convert a percentage to a letter grade.
    
    Args:
        percent: The percentage score (or None)
        
    Returns:
        The letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) or "-" if percent is None
    """
    if percent is None:
        return "-"
    elif percent >= 90:
        return "A"
    elif percent >= 80:
        return "B"
    elif percent >= 70:
        return "C"
    elif percent >= 60:
        return "D"
    else:
        return "F"

    g.set_weight("quiz", 0.3)
    g.set_weight("exam", 0.3)

    g.record("Alice", "Homework 2", 90)
    g.record("Alice", "Quiz 1", 40)
    g.record("Alice", "Exam 1", 180)
    
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 1", 70)
    g.record("Bob", "Homework 2", 75)
    g.record("Bob", "Quiz 1", 30)
    g.record("Bob", "Exam 1", 160)
    
    # Test weighted averages

    # 100th percentile should be 5.0

    entries2 = [
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 1.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 2.0},
        {'seconds': 3.0}
    ]

import re
from collections import Counter
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def parse_line(line):
    # Apache access log format: ip - - [time] "request" status bytes time
    # Example: 127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
    
    pattern = r'^(\S+) \S+ \S+ \[([^\]]+)\] "(\S+ \S+ \S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)$'
    match = re.match(pattern, line.strip())
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match expected format")
    
    ip, time, request, status, bytes_str, seconds = match.groups()
    
    # Parse request into method and path
    method, path, _ = request.split(' ')
    
    # Convert status to int
    status = int(status)
    
    # Convert bytes to int, handling "-" case
    if bytes_str == "-":
        bytes_val = 0
    else:
        bytes_val = int(bytes_str)
    
    # Convert seconds to float
    seconds = float(seconds)
    
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes_val,
        'seconds': seconds
    }
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test with the example line
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    result = parse_line(test_line)
    
    expected = {
        'ip': '127.0.0.1',
        'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
        'method': 'GET',
        'path': '/index.html',
        'status': 200,
        'bytes': 2326,
        'seconds': 0.045
    }
    
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    print("All tests passed!")
def parse_log(text):
    """Parse log text and return list of parsed dicts for valid lines."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parsed = parse_line(line)
            result.append(parsed)
        except ValueError:
            # Skip malformed lines
            continue
    
    return result

def bad_lines(text):
    """Return 1-based line numbers of malformed lines that are not blank."""
    lines = text.strip().split('\n')
    result = []
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):  # 1-based indexing
        if not line.strip():  # Skip blank lines
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            result.append(i)
    
    return result

def status_counts(entries):
    """Return a dictionary mapping status codes to their counts."""
    counts = {}
    for entry in entries:
        status = entry['status']
        counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
    return counts

def error_rate(entries):
    """Return the fraction of entries whose status is 500 or more, rounded to 4 decimals.
    
    Returns 0.0 when there are no entries.
    """
    if not entries:
        return 0.0
    
    error_count = 0
    for entry in entries:
        if entry['status'] >= 500:
            error_count += 1
    
    return round(error_count / len(entries), 4)

def top_paths(entries, n=3):
    """Return a list of (path, count) tuples for the n most requested paths.
    
    Paths with query strings are stripped of the query part.
    Ties are broken by path name (lexicographically).
    """
    # Extract paths from entries
    paths = []
    for entry in entries:
        path = entry['path']
        # Remove query string if present
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        clean_path = parsed.path
        paths.append(clean_path)
    
    # Count occurrences
    counter = Counter(paths)
    
    # Get most common items
    most_common = counter.most_common(n)
    
    # If there are ties, sort by path name
    if most_common:
        # Group by count value
        groups = {}
        for path, count in most_common:
            if count not in groups:
                groups[count] = []
            groups[count].append(path)
        
        # Sort each group lexicographically
        for count in groups:
            groups[count].sort()
        
        # Build result in order of count (descending) then path (ascending)
        result = []
        for count in sorted(groups.keys(), reverse=True):
            for path in groups[count]:
                result.append((path, count))
        
        return result
    
    return []

def percentile(entries, p):
    """Return the p-th percentile of the seconds values by nearest rank.
    
    The smallest value such that at least p percent of the values are less than or equal to it.
    Raises ValueError unless 0 < p <= 100 and there is at least one value.
    """
    if not entries:
        raise ValueError("No entries provided")
    
    if not (0 < p <= 100):
        raise ValueError("p must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 100")
    
    # Extract seconds values
    seconds_values = [entry['seconds'] for entry in entries]
    
    # Sort the values
    sorted_values = sorted(seconds_values)
    
    # Calculate the rank
    n = len(sorted_values)
    rank = (p / 100.0) * n
    
    # Find the nearest rank (smallest value such that at least p percent are <= it)
    # If rank is an integer, we want the value at that index
    # If rank is not an integer, we want the value at the next integer index
    if rank.is_integer():
        # Exact match - return the value at that index
        index = int(rank) - 1  # Convert to 0-based index
    else:
        # Round up to nearest integer to get the "nearest rank"
        index = int(rank)  # This gives us the next higher rank
    
    # Ensure index is within bounds
    if index >= n:
        index = n - 1
    
    return sorted_values[index]

    result = parse_line(test_line)

    # Test with "-" bytes
    test_line2 = '192.168.1.1 - - [11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000] "POST /api/data HTTP/1.1" 201 - 0.123'
    result2 = parse_line(test_line2)
    
    expected2 = {
        'ip': '192.168.1.1',
        'time': '11/Oct/2023:14:00:00 +0000',
        'method': 'POST',
        'path': '/api/data',
        'status': 201,
        'bytes': 0,
        'seconds': 0.123
    }
    
    assert result2 == expected2, f"Expected {expected2}, got {result2}"
    
    # Test ValueError for invalid line
    try:
        parse_line('invalid line format')
        assert False, "Should have raised ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass  # Expected
    
    # Test new parse_log function
    test_log = '''127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045
invalid line format

10.0.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2023:15:00:00 +0000] "PUT /upload HTTP/1.1" 200 1024 0.050'''
    
    parsed = parse_log(test_log)
    assert len(parsed) == 3, f"Expected 3 parsed lines, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]['ip'] == '127.0.0.1'
    assert parsed[1]['ip'] == '192.168.1.1'
    assert parsed[2]['ip'] == '10.0.0.1'
    
    # Test bad_lines function
    bad_line_nums = bad_lines(test_log)
    assert bad_line_nums == [2], f"Expected [2], got {bad_line_nums}"
    
    # Test with all blank lines
    blank_log = '''
    
    '''
    parsed_blank = parse_log(blank_log)
    assert len(parsed_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 parsed lines, got {len(parsed_blank)}"
    bad_blank = bad_lines(blank_log)
    assert len(bad_blank) == 0, f"Expected 0 bad lines, got {len(bad_blank)}"

    # Test top_paths function
    test_entries = [
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/index.html?param=value'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/api/data'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/about?filter=active'},
    ]
    
    result = top_paths(test_entries, n=3)
    # All three paths have 3 occurrences, so sort by path name
    expected = [('/about', 3), ('/contact', 3), ('/index.html', 3)]
    assert result == expected, f"Expected {expected}, got {result}"
    
    # Test with ties - should sort by path name
    test_entries_ties = [
        {'path': '/z'},
        {'path': '/a'},
        {'path': '/z'},
        {'path': '/a'},
        {'path': '/b'},
        {'path': '/b'},
    ]
    
    result_ties = top_paths(test_entries_ties, n=3)
    expected_ties = [('/a', 2), ('/b', 2), ('/z', 2)]
    assert result_ties == expected_ties, f"Expected {expected_ties}, got {result_ties}"
    
    print("All tests passed!")
    print("top_paths tests passed!")
def between(entries, start, end):
    """
    Return entries whose time t satisfies start <= t < end.
    start and end are "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" strings.
    """
    # Convert the start and end times to the format used in the log entries
    # The log format is "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
    # We'll need to parse and compare these times
    
    # For simplicity, we'll assume the entries are already sorted by time
    # and we'll do a simple string comparison since the format is consistent
    
    result = []
    for entry in entries:
        time_str = entry['time']
        # Extract just the date/time part (before the timezone)
        # Format: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000"
        # We want to compare "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" with our start/end times
        time_part = time_str.split(' ')[0]  # This gets "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        
        # Convert the log time format to a comparable format
        # We'll convert "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36" to "2023-10-10 13:55:36"
        # This is a bit tricky because we have to parse the month name
        
        # Parse the log time format
        # Example: "10/Oct/2023:13:55:36"
        # Split on ':' to separate date and time parts
        parts = time_part.split(':')
        date_part = parts[0]  # "10/Oct/2023"
        time_part = ':'.join(parts[1:])  # "13:55:36"
        
        day, month_str, year = date_part.split('/')
        hour, minute, second = time_part.split(':')
        
        # Convert month name to number
        month_map = {
            'Jan': '01', 'Feb': '02', 'Mar': '03', 'Apr': '04',
            'May': '05', 'Jun': '06', 'Jul': '07', 'Aug': '08',
            'Sep': '09', 'Oct': '10', 'Nov': '11', 'Dec': '12'
        }
        month = month_map[month_str]
        
        # Format as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
        log_time_formatted = f"{year}-{month}-{day} {hour}:{minute}:{second}"
        
        # Compare with start and end times
        if start <= log_time_formatted < end:
            result.append(entry)
    
    return result

    """Convert a percentage to a letter grade.
    
    Args:
        percent: The percentage score (or None)
        
    Returns:
        The letter grade (A, B, C, D, F) or "-" if percent is None

    if percent is None:
        return "-"
    elif percent >= 90:
        return "A"
    elif percent >= 80:
        return "B"
    elif percent >= 70:
        return "C"
    elif percent >= 60:
        return "D"
    else:
